title: Augmented strict reduction tower of ordinary pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, small pro-etale sites, coefficient sheaves $B_W=A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, and strict tower categories of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], for $W=T,T'$. Put $R_W=\underline A_W$, $S_{n,W}=\underline{P_n}_W=(P_n)_W$, and write $\operatorname{Res}_W:D(B_W)\to D(R_W)$ for exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the canonical finite coefficient comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the derived module pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

For any $K\in D(B_T)$, without a completeness hypothesis, put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{n,T}$ and $N=Lg^*_{R}\operatorname{Res}_T K$. Let $H_\bullet=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, a complex of strict $B_{T'}$-towers whose finite coefficient evaluations are $H_n=Lg_n^*K_n$. Let $\mathcal R(N)_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$ denote the strict reduction tower computed on one flat-term K-flat representative [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum, def-pc-kflat-complex].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\tau:\mathcal R(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{T'}H_\bullet$ in the derived category of strict $R_{T'}$-towers, induced by an isomorphism of strict diagrams on compatible K-flat models. Its finite coefficient evaluation is the composite $\tau_n$ of the canonical pullback/tensor comparison with $Lg_n^*$ of the finite constant-to-completed scalar comparison. It commutes with every quotient transition and carries the quotient augmentation from the constant tower on $N$ to the restriction of the pulled-back quotient augmentation, precomposed with the ordinary constant-to-completed pullback comparison.

For $\widehat N=R\lim\mathcal R(N)$, using total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], it induces an isomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Res}_{T'}(R\lim H_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat N$. If $p_n^H,p_n$ are the respective evaluations, then $\operatorname{Res}(p_n^H)=\tau_n p_n\rho$. Under $\rho$ the pulled-back augmentation gives the quotient-completion unit $\eta:N\to\widehat N$, and $p_n\eta=u_n$, the finite scalar-extension unit. All comparisons are natural in $K$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-model-descent] for the ordinary and derived comparisons, both universal-counit formulas, and the strict augmented identity.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-limit-projection-unit] for lambda. Naturality of the derived projection along tau inverse and cancellation of tau inverse followed by tau give the projection formula for limitComparison.

Naturality of lambda on the pulled augmentation and its constant-unit normalization rewrite the pulled completion comparison. Precompose with delta and apply naturality of the diagonal adjunction unit. The strict augmented identity rewrites the map inside derived limit; cancellation of tau followed by tau inverse gives the completion unit. Naturality of each derived projection along the quotient augmentation gives the final finite projection equation.

split_report.summary: Retained the statement and all imported metadata; supplied a nine-step proof using only existing nodes. The whole augmented coefficient diagram is resolved at once to identify the derived tower pullback, finite reductions use one flat-term K-flat representative, restriction preserves tower K-injectives by its exact left adjoint, and evaluations and completion units are computed on these models. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes paragraph 2 of the current completed-pullback-reduction proof: pull back the strict reduction tower and identify it with the reduction tower of ordinary constant-coefficient pullback, before finite reduction of completion. Also makes the augmentation and derived-limit evaluation normalization explicit. No chapter or unit route is changed.

tool_uses.why: Exact constant-coefficient inverse image and its ring identification on a geometric morphism are generic tools; no proper-base-change-unit statement supplies the assertion for the possibly infinite ring A.

The explicit chain-level tensor and scalar-association isomorphisms are needed before localization to keep the strict quotient diagram and its augmentation; the unit’s bifunctorial derived tensor statement alone does not supply chain formulas.
Generic scalar extension preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms; used for B tensor_R V_j, not as a replacement of the unit route.
Generic total tensor closure and reassociation for unbounded flat-term K-flat complexes are used to put E_J in the diagram resolving class.
The universal resolving-class construction descends the actual natural chain maps and augmented equalities; it is a generic derived-functor tool.
The ordinary extension/restriction adjunction supplies the exact left adjoint needed for K-injective preservation on towers.

Step 1: flat-term K-flat P; Res P stays K-flat because the completed ring is flat over the constant one; pullback preserves K-flat with no flatness of c needed. Step 2: the common-quotient node gives a strict tower iso including the cone; tensor coherence gives c_n; exact finite pullback gives T_n = Lg_n^*K_n. Step 3: the augmented category J (objects * and n≥1) is resolved strictly. This is needed because F_n is not K-flat over B. The E_j are flat-term K-flat by change-of-rings and the total-tensor-model node. Step 4: I checked by hand that g^*E_j ≅ Tot(Q⊗_C(D⊗_{R'}V'_j)). Flatness of D over R' and K-flatness of Q over C give quasi-isomorphisms onto (g^*P, T_•), because UB→D→S_n' equals U(B→S_n). Step 5: the pure-tensor identities for transitions and augmentation hold, and the source map is the scalar-extension comparison of constant-completion-equivalence. Step 6: descent through roofs via the resolving-class node. Step 7: Res' has an exact left adjoint (by flatness), so 08BJ applies levelwise on towers and lim commutes with restriction literally. Step 8: the type check gives Res'p_n^H = τ_n p_n ρ. Step 9: η comes from the units computed on the shared restricted resolution, and p_nη = u_n. Edge cases K=0, g=id, I=0 and unbounded K are all fine. The six declared tool_uses are generic tools and accepted; right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective is in sk-def-exchange, which the unit cites, so it is on the route. No SGA is cited. Minor point, not a fault: step 2 leaves implicit that P^p⊗_B S_n is flat over S_n (elementary base change).
